description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

integer-certified invariants of that dynamics:
1. SPANNING-TREE COMPLEXITY tau (Matrix-Tree theorem): tau = det of ANY principal (n-1)x(n-1)
cofactor of L, an exact positive integer. Computed by FRACTION-FREE (Bareiss) integer Gaussian

2. RANDOM-WALK RETURN COUNTS (A^k)_{ii} = number of closed walks of length k from vertex i. These
graphs are vertex-transitive: the return counts are the same at every vertex.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `seq_knowledge_uncertain`. seq_push_uncertain into a Seq<Knowledge<f64>> stores a real Knowledge element. It should compile and run successfully.
description: seq_push_uncertain into a Seq<Knowledge<f64>> stores a real Knowledge element
comments: `seq_push_uncertain` exists only in the lean_single bootstrap surface
(self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio). Madaros never implemented it: its Seq
method lowering has an explicit arm that refuses `.push_uncertain(...)`, and
the free-function spelling used here does not resolve at all, so the file
reports E137 rather than the refusal. Measured 2026-09-04 on the committed
bin/madaros-linux-x86_64; the name has no definition anywhere in the tree.
Same shape as tests/compile-fail/refinement_subtype_strict.sio: the feature
lives in the seed, so the test must not run on the Madaros job.
Regression for the Lane C SIGSEGV: seq_push_uncertain passed its raw f64 `value`
to seq_materialize_push_value, which — because type_is_struct_like(0, knowledge_hash)
is true — heap-copied 24 bytes treating the f64 bits as a Knowledge-block pointer and
crashed. The fix assembles a real Knowledge block {value@0, variance@8, confidence@16}
from the (value, confidence, variance) scalars (same representation as .push(measure(..)))
and materializes that, so per-element reads work and the additive header aggregate
(Σ variance, min confidence) is preserved. (Seq<i64>/Seq<f64> were never affected;
see seq_epistemic.sio.)

comments: Vancomycin prescription safety: compile-time ε-bound enforcement.
